newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges tax bill vote before Aug. recess.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges tax bill vote before Aug. recess.

text.p: President Clinton said he was ready to continue work in August on tax and spending bills if Congress would delay its planned month-long break, Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle said Thursday.

"I'm not going anywhere," Daschle said the president told him Wednesday night at a White House meeting on issues facing Congress. The South Dakota Democrat said there was danger that momentum behind the economic legislation would evaporate if it were held over until September.
Clinton is to vacation in Martha's Vineyard starting Aug. 17. Congress is scheduled to begin its recess Aug. 1.
"He's in no hurry. We'd rather have a good bill than a fast bill," Daschle said.

The White House meeting was held to make sure the Senate Democrats and Clinton were "on exactly the same page where our priorities are" regarding a number of issues the chamber will be considering this year.

Daschle said Clinton agreed they will insist that a child tax credit be made refundable to those who pay payroll taxes but pay little or no income tax. He said full refundability was "our current position."

On the issue of a tobacco tax to pay for children's health care, Daschle said he expected one would be passed at some level. However, it could be included in the spending bill rather than the tax bill.
